title: dedicated-autoscaler-burst-throttle-util-reporting-enhancement
author: Ayesha Kapoor
release_notes: Enhances Dedicated autoscaler reporting by adding burst throttle metrics, improved token-bucket visibility, and per-priority utilization breakdowns. No user-facing API changes.
description: Motivation: operators have limited visibility into burst throttle behavior and per-priority utilization when Dedicated fleets hit transient demand spikes. This PR adds end-to-end reporting for burst throttle events and token-bucket state so SREs and platform users can correlate throttles with throughput guarantees and autoscaler decisions. Design: 1) add a lightweight telemetry event for burst_throttle.{start|end} that includes fleet_id, priority_class, requested_tokens, granted_tokens, and current_token_bucket_level. 2) emit periodic per-fleet priority utilization summaries for the observability pipeline (1m rollups) including active_instances, queued_requests, avg_latency_ms, and token_bucket_fill_pct. 3) extend the existing dedicated_autoscaler_metrics exporter to include token_bucket_drops_total and burst_throttle_duration_seconds. 4) UI: add a new panel to the Dedicated fleet dashboard that surfaces burst throttle rate and token-bucket fill over time. Implementation notes: events are emitted from the autoscaler loop and the throttle path to minimize instrumentation overhead; metrics use pre-aggregated counters to avoid cardinality explosion; rollout is gated behind a feature flag dedicated.autoscaler.burst_reporting. Checklist: - [x] prototype telemetry schema and wire up to pipeline - [x] add metric exporter fields and Prometheus mappings - [x] update dashboard JSON and add example queries - [x] unit and integration tests for telemetry emission - [x] feature flag gating and config defaults - [x] docs PR draft linked. Testing and rollout: verified in qa cluster for 48h under load generator with configured burst windows; observed token_bucket_drops_total correlate with synthetic overloads and dashboards show expected rollups. Feature flagged by default-off; will enable in canary fleets for two weeks before global enable. Backcompat: all changes are additive and behind a flag; no breaking API changes. Related: ENG-4521 (ownership and dashboard), ENG-4580 (autoscaler improvements), SUP-1982 (customer incident demonstrating lack of visibility).
commits: add: telemetry event for burst_throttle start/end (autoscaler)
feat: export token_bucket_drops_total and burst_throttle_duration_seconds to Prometheus
feat: per-priority utilization rollups and observability exporter
docs: dashboard JSON + queries for burst throttle panel
test: unit tests for telemetry emission + integration test with observability pipeline
fix: reduce telemetry cardinality by hashing optional tags

Author reply (Ayesha Kapoor): Confirmed, fleet_id is hashed and we limit priority_class to enum values; bumped metric names to dedicated_autoscaler_token_bucket_drops_total and dedicated_autoscaler_burst_throttle_duration_seconds to follow existing prefix.

Author reply: Added dashboard README note and included an example correlating burst_throttle events with rollout tags in the observability queries section.
